chapter_note: Highly substratic chapter on the cosmic Wheel and four kinds of archonic distribution. Teaching purity 0.960, very low fatigue. The only clear editorial intrusions are the opening "Once again the Illuminator said" attribution (i=3) and the closing hortatory formula ⲁⲓ̈ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ ('I have made known to you') at the very end (i=76-77). Substantial damage (26.9%) but the surviving cosmological architecture — wheel, sphere, ten firmaments, eight earths, four places of Darkness, three strongholds, twelve zodiacs, seven guides — is all internal cosmic mapping (cosmos→cosmos). The 'king and his comitatus' in i=57-71 is the King of the realms of Darkness, internal to the system. The chapter is a clean numbered enumeration of the Four Great Works following the Persian-style structural pedagogy.
